chapter: Early freelance work and New Orleans trumpeters
title: First trumpet jobs around town: small bands, Dominguez, George Lewis
summary: Ernie lists the small groups he played with in the Depression years. They included Wooden Joe, Paul Dominguez, Simon Marrero and Harold Dejan on Decatur Street, about four years with George Lewis, and Chester Zardis's group.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You were going to go on with your life there. Excuse the interruption, he's one of the great trumpet players. We never knew him before.

Yes he was, he was very great. And like I was telling you, I started playing trumpet around here and some of the small outfits. No name outfit. I played quite a few jobs with Burbank and several jobs. And several jobs with two trumpets. I played a job with Kid Rene with Wooden Joe, you were the one with Joe Nickles. Boy I knew Wooden Joe, yeah very well. And also with Bill N. D. D. And I played a job with Paul Dominguez, the violinist. I played several jobs right there, especially during the pression. They had these little Bill Pauls was having bands, mostly on the weekends like that. And I played several jobs with Steve Lewis, Johnny Sancia, and Simon Marrero, and Steve Lewis and myself. Mostly a string outfit. Because after I know Matoyi had died, I was going to Paul Dominguez to take a few lessons with him. That was the violin player.

But he helped you with your reading you know? Yeah, he was a good musician. So when they would get a job like that, he would always cut me. And then I played some job with Willis San Diego. Doing the, out on Decatur Street during that time. Right after I left Harold, because I worked with Harold a good while on, at the Popeye on Decatur Street. He had an impression. He had an outfit out there. And I saw several jobs with George Lewis and Richard McLean and a bunch.
You stayed with George Lewis a good while ago?

Yeah, I think with George for about four years playing a different place. And then I went with Chester's Otis. Little Chester's Otis. He played bass player. He had a group with me and Howard Mandorf and Alexis Russel. You might have heard him. He's a saxophone player.
He's working with Whitney Bank there, the messenger. The same place that the bass player lived on. Eddie Dawson. Eddie Dawson. Yeah, yeah. He stopped playing music.
Yeah, I think he's one of those Jehovah's Witnesses.
Oh, maybe I did hear him.
And Homer Eugene was in that outfit too at that time, playing guitar. And another fellow, I don't know if he's right now, they call him Titi. He used to play drum with Chris Kelly one time.

Titi. He was a show drummer, but he was at the Nighthawk, crossing the car, you understand? Yeah, by the Nighthawk, yeah. That's right. When Chris Kelly was at the Gypsy Tee Room, he was over there. Yeah, I think I did hear him.
He had that Tee Room. We used to go to the Nighthawk somewhere and leave the Gypsy Tee Room at night.
That's right. You know, come over there.
